platon.paper: Schwengers et al. 2020, Microb Genom, doi:10.1099/mgen.0.000398

plasme.paper: Tang et al. 2023, Nucleic Acids Res, doi:10.1093/nar/gkad578

plasmidhunter.paper: Tian et al. 2024, Brief Bioinform, doi:10.1093/bib/bbae322
plasmidhunter.install: pip install plasmidhunter (+ conda diamond=2.1.8 prodigal)

note: Platon, MOB-suite, PLASMe and PlasmidHunter are run exactly as published, not retrained. Fragments are presented to all four grouped by assembly, i.e. as the contigs of one fragmented draft assembly, which is the input Platon and mob_recon were designed for; PLASMe and PlasmidHunter classify each contig independently, so the grouping neither helps nor hurts them and keeps the input identical across tools. Fragments are linear sub-sequences of a replicon, so they carry no circularity and usually no oriT or rep hallmark; the database- and hallmark-driven tools are therefore expected to lean chromosomal, and the replicon-level numbers are the fairer comparison.
